findings.reason: the stated requirement is a correction at two places, and as written the gate proves the first is unnecessary, so a node can deliver half the fix green; the section needs either a case whose two reviews contribute per section (so `contributing` holds both records and `read_plan_review`'s tie-break decides case one) or the matching control, "leaving `read_plan_review`'s `max` unchanged fails case one".
findings.text: the Done-when fixes one fixture shape — two reviews at the same `plan_version` — and the section's own control three ("correcting only `read_plan_review` leaves `review_coverage` returning the older review") presumes both records carry the plan's fingerprint, which is exactly the shape where `review_coverage`'s whole-plan branch returns `[newest]`, a one-element list (`plan_review.py:1024-1039`); `read_plan_review`'s `max(covering, ...)` at `:1268` therefore has nothing to choose between, so all five cases and five of the six controls pass with only the `review_coverage` site corrected and the `read_plan_review` tie-break left picking the oldest — the very site the Deliverable names first

response_events.note: §43 now adds a fixture where the two reviews' fingerprints do not match the plan, so review_coverage takes its per-section branch and returns both, and read_plan_review's max faces the tie; a case asserts it returns the newer, with a control that corrects only review_coverage.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited site resolves at this revision: `max(covering, key=plan_version)` at `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:1268`, `newest = max(whole, key=plan_version)` at `:1024`, `sorted(records, key=plan_version)` at `:1077`, `records.sort(key=(timestamp, review_path))` at `:1480`, the refusals at `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2784` and `:2792`, `def _crew(` at `reckon/mcp.py:2608` and the `_crew_write_action(` call at `:2812`; the two cited reviews exist in the nova store with the run ids the section names and both raise `wiring-1`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the five cases fix one fixture shape, and in that shape `review_coverage`'s whole-plan branch returns a single record, so the second of the two declared tie sites is measured by no case and no control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every log is under the run directory, starts with its revision and the literal command, and ends in `EXIT=`; the new test lives under `tests/`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches a symbol, file name or comment, and the new test file is named for the rule it checks.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the evidence: `max` over a list ordered oldest-first returns the oldest of a tie (`plan_review.py:1268`, `:1024`), the answer verb builds its covering set from `(record, design)` in `crew_review` at `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2770-2799` so `--review-run` cannot name a newer review, and `mcp_crew_actions.py`'s `answer` argument map and defaults carry no `review_run`; each mechanism runs on a production caller the section names (`routing.py:2717` and `:2721`, `crew review --answer`, the `crew` tool's `_crew`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the tie-break at two sites, the widened `--review-run`, the MCP parameter and the residual ambiguity refusal all serve the one goal, an answer reaching the newest review that raised the finding.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §43 declares no dependency, and no other implementable section (§37, §39) writes `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` or `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py`, so nothing it needs is unordered; the sections that share those files (§41, §42) are `done`, and the gate readers it cites (`routing.py` near 2717/2721) are read-only callers, not write paths.
